title: skip
summary: A programming language to skip the things you have already computed Skip is a general-purpose programming language that tracks side effects to provide caching with reactive invalidation, ergonomic and safe parallelism, and efficient garbage collection. Skip is statically typed and ahead-of-time compiled using LLVM to produce highly optimized executables. Skip's main new language feature is its precise tracking of side effects, including both mutability of values as well as distinguishing between non-deterministic data sources and those that can provide reactive invalidations telling Skip when data has changed. When Skip's type system can prove the absence of side effects at a given function boundary developers can opt-in to safely memoizing that computation, with the runtime ensuring that previously cached values are invalidated when underlying data changes.
